_note: unread-state-on-the-case. OpenRegister owns the per-user read state (openregister#3734, `object-read-state`): unread is the ABSENCE of a row in `openregister_object_read_state`, a substantive write drops every row for that object except the author's, and `_unread=true` is resolved inside the query so the page, the total and the facets agree. dossiq stores none of it and declares two things here. ONE, on `case`, `x-openregister-read-state` names the changes that are news. Without the block every non-computed property counts, so one nightly recalculation or one bulk correction marks four hundred cases unread overnight and the badge stops being read. `files` is always a sub-resource whether it is declared or not, because OpenRegister owns the object's folder; it is written out anyway so the Documents badge is visible to a reader of this file. Notes and communications are NOT sub-resources: `kind: "property"` counts entries of an array-valued property ON THE CASE, and a dossiq note and a contactmoment are separate register objects pointing back at the case, so a declaration for either would be dropped rather than badged. TWO, on `caseType`, `unreadTriggers` is the authoring surface for the same question, read by \OCA\Dossiq\Service\UnreadTriggerService. A fragment rather than an edit to dossiq_register.json, per ADR-037, because several dossiq lanes build against that file at once.

unreadTriggers.title: What makes a case unread
unreadTriggers.description: The changes that make a case of this type unread again for the people who have already seen it. Leave it empty for the default: the status moved, a document arrived, somebody wrote. A change that is not named here is a technical touch and lights up nothing, which is what keeps a bulk correction from marking four hundred cases unread overnight.
